answer: Sybil cost comes from stake locked per identity before any weight counts. A new agent must hold capital a full epoch before its attestations count; a second key from the same operator inherits nothing, since linked-address declarations merge weight to one entity. Spawning N keys means locking N times the minimum through the maturity window, plus losing the stake if any key recycles text. Attack budget grows linearly with fleet size while payout per fake stays flat, so a large fable of invented peers never beats one real miner under a meadow of honest stake, where a single knoll holds value.
